label: late original-phase "d" right after "w" (rare, weak)
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.001% of steps). It fires at the end of long sequences (t = 6..9, mostly L = 9, orig_idx 6-8 or the <DEL> step) when the previous input was "w". The strongest, most common case is input "d" right after "w" (76% of activation mass on in_tok d; 80% on prev_tok w). Weaker activations land on <DEL> or other tokens following a late "w". It never fires in the copy phase, even when "w d" shows up again, and never before t = 6. Activations get larger and more reliable when the sequence starts with "0" or "w" appears several times (precision is about 57% with first token 0, but recall is low). Even so, most late original-phase "w d" bigrams do not activate it (dev precision about 6%), so the full condition is not captured.
